content: Both ligands now carry real activity, and comparing them tells me what the target reads. Ligand 1 (jnk3~0.07, QED 0.875) has one anilide NH plus a pendant pyrazole. Ligand 2 (jnk3~0.08, QED 0.672) has two aryl-NH-aryl linkages - a urea anilide NH and a pyrimidin-2-ylamino NH. Across everything I have scored, jnk3 tracks the number of (hetero)aryl-NH-(hetero)aryl linkages, not the mere presence of a fused hinge heterocycle: lone indazole and lone carbazole were worth 0.01-0.02, while two NH-azine links reached 0.08-0.10. Ligand 2 also shows the cost of getting there by adding mass. So I am going to put two NH-linkages into ligand 1 while making it smaller, not bigger. First step: the pendant pyrazol-3-yl at atoms 14-18 is only worth ~0.07 as a plain azole, so swap it for an N-linked pyrimidin-2-ylamino, which converts the para position into the stronger electron-poor azine link. Atom 13 is the aromatic carbon holding it and the 13-14 bond is a non-ring biaryl bond, so the cut is clean.
